_note: Optional layer on top of events.json: what activists, influencers and pro-government voices posted around the Finance Bill 2024. Same format as events.json, so both simulators can add it to the news timeline. Accounts are fictional composites; no real person is named or imitated. Each post paraphrases the kind of content that circulated publicly on that date (explainers, MPs' phone numbers, #RejectFinanceBill2024 / #OccupyParliament calls, pro-bill messaging); the wording is ours. Posts never say which counties protested, so protest geography stays a validation target. Used to compare a news-only information environment with one that includes the online mobilisation.

events.text: [6 June 2024] Finance Bill 2024 kwa lugha rahisi: 16% VAT on bread means a loaf goes up by about Sh10. Eco levy hits sanitary pads and diapers. 2.5% motor vehicle tax every year. Higher excise on M-Pesa fees. Read it before your MP votes. #RejectFinanceBill2024
[12 June 2024] Your MP's phone number is public. Call or SMS them today and tell them to vote NO on the Finance Bill. They work for us. #RejectFinanceBill2024
[15 June 2024] New skit: a family counts coins for bread, data and pads after the Finance Bill. 'Mkate ni anasa sasa' (bread is a luxury now). Share if you are tired. #RejectFinanceBill2024
[16 June 2024] The Finance Bill reduces borrowing and funds teachers, health and roads. Much of what is trending is misinformation. The committee is already listening to the public on bread.
[17 June 2024] Tomorrow we #OccupyParliament. Peaceful. Wear black, carry water, film everything. Nairobi CBD, 10am. If you cannot come, call your MP.
[18 June 2024] They dropped bread VAT to calm us down, but the bill still raises taxes to pay debt. Amendments are a distraction. Thursday: protests in every town. #RejectFinanceBill2024
[18 June 2024] The government has listened: no VAT on bread, no motor vehicle tax, no new mobile money charges. Time to move forward together.
[20 June 2024] Today Kenyans marched in Nairobi and in towns across the country, young people from every community. Teargas will not silence us. #OccupyParliament
[21 June 2024] Tuesday 25th June: total shutdown. Third reading day. Everyone, everywhere. #OccupyEverywhere #RejectFinanceBill2024
[22 June 2024] Our new song 'Reject' is for every boda rider, mama mboga and student who is tired. See you Tuesday. #RejectFinanceBill2024
[23 June 2024] The President says he is ready to engage the youth. Peaceful protest is a right, but criminals are hijacking demonstrations. Stay home and stay safe.
[25 June 2024] Police are shooting at protesters. Share first-aid contacts and lawyers' numbers. Do not let them say we were criminals. #OccupyParliament
[26 June 2024] Withdrawing the bill is not enough. Justice for those killed. Thursday we march again.
